verses.1: And the LORD said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid. Do not take along with you all the people who are going into battle. But rise up and go ahead. I have given you in your hands the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.”
verses.2: And you made her queen, just as you did with Jericho and its king. You took her away from her city, so that she would no longer be able to rule over it.
verses.3: And Joshua and all the people who were fighting stood up. Joshua selected thirty thousand men, the leaders of the army, and sent them out at night.
verses.4: And he commanded them, “See that you approach the city from behind it. Do not go too far away from the city; instead, stay close to it.”
verses.5: And I, along with all the people who were with me, rushed towards the city. It was as if they had come out to greet us, just as they did in the past.
verses.6: And they went after us, trying to get them out of the city. They said, “Miracles have happened before us, just as they did in the past.”
verses.7: And you shall inherit the city from those who were before you. Jehovah your God will give it into your hands.
verses.8: And they shall set fire to the city. They shall burn the city with fire, as Jehovah has commanded. See, I have given you this commandment.
verses.9: And Joshua sent them away. They went to the wilderness and settled among the houses of El and between the valleys of the sea. That night, Joshua slept among the people.
verses.10: And Joshua arose in the morning, and he led the people. He stood before the people of Israel.
verses.11: And all the people who fought, those who went up to them and came towards the city. They camped at the foot of the hills, between them and the city.
verses.12: And he took five thousand men, and he put them in charge of guarding between the house of El and the sea.
verses.13: And the people set up all the camps that were located near the city, as well as those camps that were located along the shore from the sea to the city. And Joshua went there at night, through the darkness.
verses.14: And there was a vision of the king of Assyria. They rushed forward, rushed out, and the people of the city went out to call upon Israel for help in battle. And all the people gathered together before sunset. But he did not know that he was surrounded by enemies from outside the city.
verses.15: And Joshua and all of Israel bowed down before them. They then crossed over the Jordan River.
verses.16: And all the people who were with them cried out in despair. They pursued Yehoshua, and they separated from the city.
verses.17: And no one remained in Ai and in the house of God. They did not follow after Israel. They abandoned the city of Peor and pursued after Israel.
verses.18: And the LORD said to Joshua, “Hold your staff in your hand. I will give you the city into your hands.” So Joshua held his staff in his hand and went towards the city.
verses.19: And the angel quickly rose from his place. He stretched out his arms, and the city was captured. They rushed in and set fire to the city.
verses.20: And the people of Ai turned around and saw that smoke was rising from the city in the sky. They didn’t have any hands to help them at that moment. The people of Shechem became desperate.
verses.21: Josue and all of Israel saw that the city was completely destroyed. Smoke rose from the city, and they returned and attacked the people of Ai.
verses.22: And these people came out of the city to be called. They became part of Israel’s army. Some of them were killed, and some were left alive.
verses.23: And they released the king of Ai alive. They brought him before Jehosua.
verses.24: And it happened that Israel killed all those who lived in the fields along the coast, those whom they had been chasing. They all died from the arrows. Then all of Israel returned to their homes, and they burned them down completely.
verses.25: And on that day, there were twenty-two thousand men and women who fell. All of those people from the city were killed.
verses.26: And Joshua did not return his hand that was raised in anger, until he had put an end to all those who were sitting on the throne.
verses.27: Only the cattle and the goods of that city were taken away from them by Israel, as Jehovah commanded Joshua.
verses.28: And Joshua destroyed that city. It became a desolate place, and it remains so to this day.
verses.29: And the king of Ai was hanged on that tree until evening came. When the sun set, Joshua ordered that the noose be removed from the tree. They then threw it outside the city gates. There, they built a large stone wall around it, as we see to this day.
verses.30: Then Joshua will build a altar for the LORD, the God of Israel, on the mountain of Ebal.
verses.31: When Moses commanded the servants of Jehovah, “Let them make offerings to God,” as written in Moses’ Book of Regulations, they made offerings of stone vessels that were not covered with brass. They placed these vessels on altars and offered sacrifices to God.
verses.32: And he wrote on the stones the laws of Moses, which he had written before the children of Israel.
verses.33: And all of Israel, along with their elders and judges, stood here. They stood facing the priests who were carrying the Ark of the Covenant of Jehovah. The Ark was carried halfway up Mount Gerizim, and then halfway up Mount Ebal. This was as Moses commanded the servants of Jehovah, so that they might bless the people of Israel at that time.
verses.34: And after that, he read out all the words of the Torah, both those that are blessed and those that are cursed, just as they were written in the book of the Torah.
verses.35: There was nothing that Moses commanded that Yehoshua did against all the people of Israel, women, children, and foreigners who lived among them.
